name: tpu
description: Weight-stationary systolic matrix-multiply tile, in the style of the Google TPU matrix-multiply unit (MXU).
authorship: Zero ASIC Corporation; author Andreas Olofsson

human_review.notes: Provenance (model and date) confirmed by the author; architecture, scope, and verification were directed and reviewed by the author.

spec.summary: Synthesizable, technology-agnostic 8x8 weight-stationary systolic matrix-multiply accelerator in the style of the Google TPU MXU. The benchmark top tpu computes one tile product C = A * B, where A and B are N x N signed int8 matrices and C is N x N signed int32 (defaults N = 8, DW = 8, ACCW = 32). B is the weight matrix, loaded into and held stationary in the processing elements; A is the activation matrix, streamed through the array, with results draining out the bottom. The design is a 2D mesh of N x N identical tpu_pe cells (assembled by tpu_array and wrapped by tpu), each holding one stationary weight and performing the only arithmetic: a signed DW x DW multiply and an ACCW-bit accumulate. The streaming wrapper adds the input skew and output de-skew shift registers needed to time-align the systolic data flow, so a result row appears 2*N-1 cycles after its activation row was accepted. The interface is a single streamed tile over a generic valid-based handshake (w_valid/w_data load phase, a_valid/a_data compute phase, c_valid/c_data result), with no on-chip RAM and no AXI.
key_decisions: Weight-stationary mapping: weights B are loaded into and held in the PEs, activations A stream west-to-east, and partial sums accumulate north-to-south, the canonical TPU MXU dataflow.
Fixed 8x8 (N = 8) 64-PE array as the default with TPU int8 x int8 -> int32 datatype (DW = 8, ACCW = 32); N, DW, and ACCW are parameters.
int8 signed MAC per PE: a single signed DW x DW multiply plus an ACCW-bit add, with signedness isolated to the multiply via $signed() so part-selects do not strip the sign.
Per-element hardware is modeled with generate (one tpu_pe per element, one shift-register stage per skew tap); no procedural unroll of the WIN x WIN array.
Generic valid-based streaming interface (w_valid/a_valid/c_valid), not AXI or any bus protocol, keeping the block self-contained.
No on-chip RAM: a single tile streams through, so there are no large buffers and no BRAM, avoiding block-RAM mapping pitfalls.

origin.notes: Original implementation written for LogikBench; follows the cited algorithm/standard and hardware architectures, not copied from any specific HDL source.

references: N. P. Jouppi et al., 'In-Datacenter Performance Analysis of a Tensor Processing Unit,' ISCA 2017.
H. T. Kung and C. E. Leiserson, 'Systolic Arrays (for VLSI),' in Sparse Matrix Proceedings, 1978.
